The Price Distribution Function extends this by introducing temporal dynamics—short-run fluctuations and long-run trends—captured through marginal productivity and time-dependent scarcity. Secular Change Oratory introduces macroeconomic evolution, modeling how persistent shifts in population, capital, and technology alter fundamental equilibria. These primitives form a triadic structure: static constraints (value), dynamic pricing (price), and long-term evolution (change). Their interplay defines the core operational space for GSI's Bayesian inference and GSE’s situational reasoning engines. Failure modes include equilibrium breakdowns due to exogenous shocks or misaligned expectations, which manifest as volatility spikes or structural shifts beyond model capacity.
